definition: EN: A flat slab forming the uppermost member or division of the capital of a column.
n. 荣誉, 赞美, 骑士爵位的授予礼, 连谱号
EN: A sculptural embellishment of an arch.
n. 走廊, 侧廊, 过道
EN: The subsidiary space alongside the body of a building, separated from it by columns, piers, or posts.
EN: The posts or pillars on either side of a doorway or entrance of a Greek temple – the slightly projecting piers which terminate the side walls (of the naos).
EN: The space enclosed in a church between the outer gate or railing of the rood screen and the door of the screen.
EN: 1. A raised panel below a window or wall monument or tablet.
n. (教堂)半圆形拱顶附带建筑

EN: A vaulted semicircular or polygonal end of a chancel or chapel. That portion of a church, usually Christian, beyond the "crossing" and opposite the nave. In some churches, the choir is seated in this space.
EN: A style of intercolumniation in which the distance between columns is at least four diameters. The large interval between columns necessitates the use of a wooden architrave.
EN: An architectural term applied to a colonnade, in which the intercolumniation is alternately wide and narrow.
n. 拱廊, 拱形建筑物, 有拱廊的街道
EN: A passage or walkway covered over by a succession of arches or vaults supported by columns. Blind arcade or arcading: the same applied to the wall surface.
n. 拱门, 拱形, 足弓
a. 主要的, 调皮的, 傲慢无礼的, 狡猾的
EN: A curved structure capable of spanning a space while supporting significant weight.
n. 柱顶过梁, 门窗的头线条板
EN: A formalized lintel, the lowest member of the classical entablature. Also the moulded frame of a door or window (often borrowing the profile of a classical architrave).
EN: In Georgian architecture, the small paved yard giving entry, via "area steps", to the basement floor at the front of a terraced house.
EN: A sharp edge created when two surfaces converge; this includes the raised edge between two flutes on a column or pilaster, if that edge is sharp.
EN: A type of rail, often wooden, with a cross-section resembling an isosceles triangle.
EN: A thin vertical aperture in a fortification through which an archer can launch arrows.
n. 关节, 接合, 连贯, 发音, 表达
EN: The manner or method of jointing parts such that each part is clear and distinct in relation to the others, even though joined.
EN: Masonry of large blocks cut with even faces and square edges.
EN: A moulding profile composed of a half-round surface surrounded by two flat planes (fillets).
n. 地图集, 图表集
[计] 自动测试和负载分析系统
EN: A support sculpted in the form of a man, which may take the place of a column, a pier or a pilaster.
EN: (plural: atria) The inner court of a Roman house; in a multi-story building, a toplit covered court rising through all stories.
EN: A small top story within a roof above the uppermost ceiling. The story above the main entablature of a classical façade.
n. 似阳台的窗外栏杆
EN: A false balcony, or railing at the outer plane of a window.
EN: An architectural ornament in the form of a ball inserted in the cup of a flower, which came into use in the latter part of the 13th, and was in great vogue in the early part of the 14th century.
n. 栏杆的支柱, 栏杆

EN: A small moulded shaft, square or circular, in stone or wood, sometimes metal, supporting the coping of a parapet or the handrail of a staircase. A series of balusters supporting a handrail or coping is called a balustrade.

EN: A structural member of inadequate capacity for its load or span that is augmented by one or two steel bars anchored to each bearing end at or above the centroid of the girder to assume the tension forces. The bar(s) runs down and below the girder and stand off the girder on one or more struts anchored to the girder at its bottom surface. The struts are sized to accept the compressive forces imposed without bending. The load limit to this member is the crippling capacity (horizontal failure) of the girder.
EN: A board fastened to the projecting gables of a roof.
EN: An architectural element formed by the extrusion of a single curve (or pair of curves, in the case of a pointed barrel vault) along a given distance.
n. 城堡的箭塔, 顶塔
EN: An overhanging, wall-mounted turret projecting from the walls, usually at the corners, of medieval fortifications or churches.
EN: Usually the lowest, subordinate storey of building, generally either entirely or partially below ground level; the lowest part of classical elevation, below the piano nobile.
n. 长方形廊柱大厅, 长方形教堂

EN: Originally a Roman, large roofed hall erected for transacting business and disposing of legal matters; later the term came to describe an aisled building with a clerestory. Medieval cathedral plans were a development of the basilica plan type.
EN: The lights in the upper part of a perpendicular window, abated, or only half the width of those below.
EN: An upwardly receding slope of a wall or column.
EN: A parapet (i.e., a defensive low wall between chest-height and head-height), in which rectangular gaps or indentations occur at intervals to allow for the discharge of arrows or other missiles.
n. 凹进处;吠声;桂冠;堤;港湾(bay的复数)

EN: The internal compartments of a building, each divided from the other by subtle means such as the boundaries implied by divisions marked in the side walls (columns, pilasters, etc.) or the ceiling (beams, etc.). Also, the external divisions of a building by fenestration (windows).

EN: A window of one or more storeys projecting from the face of a building. Canted: with a straight front and angled sides. Bow window: curved. Oriel: rests on corbels or brackets and starts above ground level; also the bay window at the dais end of a medieval great hall.
EN: A chamber or stage in a tower where bells are hung. The term is also used to describe the manner in which bricks are laid in a wall so that they interlock.
EN: A stone seat which runs round the walls of large churches, and sometimes round the piers; it very generally is placed in the porches.
n. 捆绑物, 结合, 债券, 契约, 粘合剂, 保证人, 键, 关栈保留
vt. 存入关栈, 使黏合
EN: Brickwork with overlapping bricks. Types of bond include stretcher, English, header, Flemish, garden wall, herringbone, basket, American, and Chinese.
n. 老板, 上司, 岩瘤, 浮雕, 母牛
vt. 指挥, 控制, 浮雕
EN: 1. A roughly cut stone set in place for later carving.
凸面装饰, 浮雕装饰

EN: Uncut stone that is laid in place in a building, projecting outward from the building, to later be carved into decorative mouldings, capitals, arms, etc. Bossages are also rustic work, consisting of stones which seem to advance beyond the surface of the building, by reason of indentures, or channels left in the joinings; used chiefly in the corners of buildings, and called rustic quoins. The cavity or indenture may be round, square, chamfered, beveled, diamond-shaped, or enclosed with a cavetto or listel.

EN: A type of support. An arc-boutant, or flying buttress, serves to sustain a vault, and is self-sustained by some strong wall or massive work. A pillar boutant is a large chain or jamb of stone, made to support a wall, terrace, or vault. The word is French, and comes from the verb bouter, "to butt" or "abut".
EN: A weight-bearing member made of wood, stone, or metal that overhangs a wall.
EN: (literally "breast- beam") A large, horizontal beam supporting the wall above, especially in a jettied building.
EN: Projecting fins or canopies which shade windows from direct sunlight.

EN: A style of pediment in which the center is left open (and often ornamented) by stopping the sloping sides short of the pediment's apex. A variant of this in which the sides are curved to resemble esses is called a swan's neck pediment.
EN: Either a small oval window, or an early type of window glass.
n. 保障, 壁垒, 防波堤

EN: A Barricade of beams and soil used in 15th- and 16th-century fortifications designed to mount artillery. On board ships the term refers to the woodwork running round the ship above the level of the deck. Figuratively it means anything serving as a defence. Dutch loanword; Bolwerk
n. 拱壁, 扶壁, 支持物
vt. 支持, 以扶壁支撑

EN: A vertical member projecting from a wall to stabilize it or to resist the lateral thrust of an arch, roof, or vault. A flying buttress transmits the thrust to a heavy abutment by means of an arch or half-arch.

EN: (plural: Cancelli) Barriers which correspond to the modern balustrade or railing, especially the screen dividing the body of a church from the part occupied by the ministers hence chancel. The Romans employed cancelli to partition off portions of the courts of law.
n. 伪善之言, 黑话, 斜面, 角落
EN: An angled (oblique) line or surface, especially one that cuts off a corner.
EN: An unsupported overhang acting as a lever, like a flagpole sticking out of the side of a wall.
n. 首都, 大写字母, 资本
a. 首都的, 重要的
EN: The topmost member of a column (or pilaster).
EN: A sculpted female figure serving as an architectural support taking the place of a column or a pillar supporting an entablature on her head.
EN: A window hung vertically, hinged one side, so that it swings inward or outward.
EN: Stalks (eight in number) with two leaves from which rise the helices or spiral scrolls of the Corinthian capital to support the abacus.
EN: A moulding in which the negative space makes a quarter-circle.
[医] 小房, 小室, 细胞
EN: The inner chamber of a temple in classical architecture.

EN: In Roman architecture, the vestibule or portico of a public building opening on to the forum, as in the basilica of Eumachia at Pompeii, and the basilica of Constantine at Rome, where it was placed at one end. See: Lacunar.
EN: A transitional edge, often 45 degrees, formed by paring down an arris diagonally. Some buildings may be chamfered such that the base is octagonal.
EN: In church architecture, the space around the altar at the east end of a traditional Christian church building, including the choir and sanctuary.
EN: The circular or horseshoe arch that decorates many Indian cave temples and shrines.

EN: In Japanese architecture, a V-shaped finial used almost exclusively on Shinto shrines, where they are placed near the ends of the ridgeline(s) of the roof through extension of or attachment to the gable. In most cases, the direction of the cut at the top of a chigi indicates the sex of the kami within.
n. 客迈拉(狮头、羊身、蛇尾的吐火女怪), 假想的妖怪, 妄想
EN: A fantastic, mythical or grotesque figure used for decorative purposes.
EN: A structure which provides ventilation.
EN: A chamber between the pronaos and the cella in Greek temples where oracles were delivered.
n. 围绕, 围绕物, 束带
vt. 以带束住, 环绕
EN: A ring, list, or fillet at the top and bottom of a column, which divides the shaft from the capital and base.
n. 十六世纪意大利的文艺

EN: A style which became prevalent in Italy in the century following 1500, now usually called 16th-century work. It was the result of the revival of classic architecture known as Renaissance, but the change had commenced already a century earlier, in the works of Ghiberti and Donatello in sculpture, and of Brunelleschi and Alberti in architecture.
n. (古罗马、希腊的)纪念碑石

EN: (plural: cippi) A low, round or rectangular pedestal set up by the Romans for military purposes such as a milestone or a boundary post. The inscriptions on some cippi in the British Museum show that they were occasionally used as funeral memorials.
n. 流通, 循环, 发行量
EN: Describes the flow of people throughout a building.
EN: A covered Greek temple, in contradistinction to hypaethral, which designates one that is uncovered; the roof of a cleithral temple completely covers it.
n. 天窗, 高侧窗, 长廊, 楼座, 火车车厢顶的通风部分
EN: The upper part of the nave of a large church, containing a series of windows.
EN: A gable or facade with a decorative shape characteristic of traditional Dutch architecture. The top of the gable is shaped like a church bell.
EN: A sunken panel in the shape of a square, rectangle, or octagon that serves as a decorative device, usually in a ceiling or vault. Also called caissons, or lacunar.

EN: (also colarino, collarino, or hypotrachelium) The little frieze of the capital of the Tuscan and Doric column placed between the astragal and the annulets. It was called hypotrachelium by Vitruvius.
n. 专栏, 圆柱, 纵队, 列, 柱形物
EN: A structural element that transmits, through compression, the weight of the structure above to other structural elements below.
n. 指南针, 范围, 音域
vt. 包围, 达到, 图谋, 理解
EN: In carpentry, architecture, and shipbuilding, a compass is a curved circular form.
EN: The Latin term for the open space left in the roof of the atrium of a Roman house (domus) for lighting it and the rooms round.
n. 墙压顶, 顶部, 顶盖, 墙的顶部
EN: The capping or covering of a wall.
EN: A structural piece of stone, wood or metal jutting from a wall to carry a superincumbent weight.
EN: A series of steps along the slopes of a gable. Also called crow-steps. A gable featuring corbiesteps is known as a corbie gable, crow-step gable, or stepped gable.

EN: One of the three orders or organisational systems of Ancient Greek or classical architecture characterised by columns which stood on the flat pavement of a temple with a base, their vertical shafts fluted with parallel concave grooves topped by a capital decorated with acanthus leaves, that flared from the column to meet an abacus with concave sides at the intersection with the horizontal beam that they carried.
EN: The upper section of an entablature or a projecting shelf along the top of a wall often supported by brackets or corbels.
n. 课程, 路线, 过程, 一道菜, 道路
EN: A layer of the same unit running horizontally in a wall.
EN: Ornamentation along the ridge of a roof.
EN: A block from which the diagonal ribs of a vault spring or start. The top of the springer is known as the skewback.
EN: A wing attached to a main or original house block, its axis at right angles to the original block, and often gabled.
n. 土窖, 地穴, 地下室
[医] 隐窝; 滤泡, 腺管
EN: A stone chamber beneath the floor of a church or other building. It typically contains coffins, sarcophagi, or religious relics.

EN: A concealed or covered passage, generally underground, though lighted and ventilated from the open air. One of the best-known examples is the crypto-porticus under the palaces of the Caesars in Rome. In Hadrian's Villa in Rome they formed the principal private intercommunication between the several buildings.
EN: A wedge-shaped division of the Roman theatre separated by the scalae or stairways. This shape also occurred in medieval architecture.
n. 圆屋顶, 圆顶篷, 圆顶的塔
[化] 化铁炉; 圆顶炉; 圆顶鼓风炉
EN: A small, most often dome-like, structure on top of a building.

EN: A projecting moulding whose edge forms an S-curve. The two major types of cyma are the cyma recta, in which the upper curve is concave, and the cyma reversa (also known as the ogee), in which the lower curve is concave.
EN: A circular projecting portico with columns.
n. 锯齿状, 小牙饰
EN: Finely toothed or notched; having dentils.
EN: One of a series of small rectangular blocks projecting from a moulding or beneath a cornice. A string of dentils is known as dentillation.
a. 柱间距离等于柱径三倍的,长距列柱式的
EN: An intercolumniation of three or four diameters.

EN: Peristyle around the great court of the palaestra, described by Vitruvius, which measured two stadia (1,200 ft.) in length, on the south side this peristyle had two rows of columns, so that in stormy weather the rain might not be driven into the inner part. The word was also used in ancient Greece for a foot race of twice the usual length.
EN: A horizontal aisle in an ancient Greek theater that separates the lower and upper tiers of semi-circular seating and intersects with the vertical aisles.
EN: An Islamic architectural term for the tribune raised upon columns, from which the Koran is recited and the prayers intoned by the Imam of the mosque.
a. [生]双翅类的, 有双廊的,四周双列柱廊式的
EN: Temples which have a double range of columns in the peristyle, as in the temple of Diana at Ephesus.
n. 十二柱式adj.十二柱式的
EN: A temple where the portico has twelve columns in front, as in the portico added to the Temple of Demeter at Eleusis, designed by Philo, the architect of the arsenal at the Peiraeus.
多利克柱式(古希腊建筑风格之一)

EN: One of the three orders or organisational systems of Ancient Greek or classical architecture characterised by columns which stood on the flat pavement of a temple without a base, their vertical shafts fluted with parallel concave grooves topped by a smooth capital that flared from the column to meet a square abacus at the intersection with the horizontal beam that they carried.
n. 老虎窗;屋顶采光窗

EN: A structural element of a building that protrudes from the plane of a sloping roof surface. Dormers are used, either in original construction or as later additions, to create usable space in the roof of a building by adding headroom and usually also by enabling addition of windows.

EN: A cubical block of stone above the capitals in a Byzantine church, used to carry the arches and vault, the springing of which had a superficial area greatly in excess of the column which carried them.
EN: A plan for a structure that is two rooms deep but lacking a central corridor.
n. 通往地底古墓或古庙的地道

EN: An entrance passage or avenue leading to a building, tomb or passageway. Those leading to beehive tombs are enclosed between stone walls and sometimes in-filled between successive uses of the tomb. In ancient Egypt the dromos was a straight, paved avenue flanked by sphinxes.
EN: A gable whose sides have a shape made up of one or more curves and has a pediment at the top.
EN: An element of Classical Revival architecture in American domestic architecture.
EN: An ornamental moulding in which an ovolo is inscribed with alternating oval and V-shaped motifs.
n. 纵向射击, 易受纵射的位置
EN: A row of rooms with aligned doorways, creating a linear processional route. Enfilades were common in upper-class Baroque architecture and are used in museum layouts to manage flow.
EN: A column built into and partially projecting from a wall, particularly notable in Roman architecture.
EN: In Japanese architecture, a section of floor outside the shoji that encircles the structure's rooms, similar to a porch or, when itself enclosed by storm doors or sheet glass, a sunroom.
n. 柱顶线盘, 柱上楣构
EN: A superstructure of mouldings and bands which lie horizontally above columns, resting on their capitals.
n. 圆柱收分曲线, 柱上的微凸线

EN: The application of a convex curve to a surface for aesthetic purposes. Its best-known use is in certain orders of Classical columns that curve slightly as their diameter is decreased from the bottom upward. It also may serve an engineering function regarding strength.
n. (古希腊,古罗马建筑里的)体操场

EN: (ephebion) A large hall in the ancient Palaestra furnished with seats, the length of which should be a third larger than the width. It served for the exercises of youths of from sixteen to eighteen years of age.
n. 古希腊寺庙内殿之后室

EN: An open vestibule behind the nave. The term is not found in any classic author, but is a modern coinage, originating in Germany, to differentiate the feature from the opisthodomos, which in the Parthenon was an enclosed chamber.
EN: In Churrigueresque Baroque architecture, an elaborate pilaster with a tapered base.
EN: The French term for a raised platform or dais. In the Levant, the estrade of a divan is called a Sopha, from which comes our word 'sofa'.
EN: Intercolumniation defined by Vitruvius as being of the best proportion, i.e. two and a quarter diameters.
n. 建筑物的正面, 外观, 表面
EN: An exterior side of a building, usually the front.
EN: A window, semicircular or semi-elliptical in shape, with glazing bars or tracery sets radiating out like an open fan.
扇形拱顶, 扇形穹顶

EN: A conoid architectural element in which a series of equidistant curved ribs projects radially from a central axis, often a vertical wall support such as a column. Fan vaults are particularly connected with the English Gothic style.
EN: 1. A board attached to the lower ends of rafters at the eaves. Along with the soffit, the fascia helps enclose the eave.
EN: An enclosure or chapel within which the fereter shrine, or tomb (as in Henry VII's chapel), was placed.
EN: 1. A small band, either raised or sunken and usually square, used to separate mouldings.

EN: An element marking the top or end of some object — such as a dome, tower, or gable — often formed to be a decorative feature. Small finials may also be used as ornamentation for furniture, poles, and light fixtures.

EN: The decorative combination on the same flat plane of flint and ashlar stone. It is characteristic of medieval buildings, most of the survivors churches, in several areas of Southern England, but especially East Anglia. If the stone projects from a flat flint wall, the term is proudwork as the stone stands "proud" rather than being "flush" with the wall.
EN: A type of buttress that transmits the thrust to a heavy abutment by means of a half-arch.

EN: An exposed structural beam over the uppermost part of a building which is not otherwise connected to the building at its highest point. A feature of H frame constructed concrete buildings and some modern skyscrapers.
n. 箔, 烘托, 衬托
vt. 贴箔于, 衬托, 阻止, 挡开, 挫败

EN: An architectural device based on a symmetrical rendering of leaf shapes, defined by overlapping circles of the same diameter that produce a series of cusps to make a lobe. Typically, the number of cusps can be three (trefoil), four (quatrefoil), five (cinquefoil), or a larger number.
EN: The area on a plane directly beneath a structure, that has the same perimeter as the structure.
EN: The lower part of a pier. (A literal translation of "pedestal.")
EN: The French term for the wall-rib carrying the web or filling-in of a vault.
EN: A coping, often ornamental, on a gable that hides the slope of the roof and becomes a parapet.
n. 日式房屋中的拉阖门

EN: An opaque partition consisting of a cloth or paper sheet over a wood framework, commonly seen in traditional Japanese architecture. Fusuma are built to be moved (usually by sliding them along tracks) or removed, allowing rooms to be reorganized and reshaped as desired and, in earlier constructions, allowing the interior of a structure to open directly to the outdoors. Some fusuma are painted, though many now feature printed graphics. Shoji are similar to fusuma but are generally translucent.
n. 山形墙, 人字板
EN: A triangular portion of an end wall between the edges of a sloping roof.

EN: Triangular terminations to buttresses, much in use in the Early English and Decorated periods, after which the buttresses generally terminated in pinnacles. The Early English gablets are generally plain, and very sharp in pitch. In the Decorated period they are often enriched with paneling and crockets. They are sometimes finished with small crosses, but more often with finials.
n. 圆模雕刻装饰;卵形或杏仁形刻纹
vt. 饰串珠状缘饰于...;饰凹槽装饰于...
EN: A carved or curved moulding used in architecture and interior design as a decorative motif, often consisting of flutes which are inverted and curved. Popular during the Italian Renaissance.
EN: The process in which the gallets or small splinters of stone are inserted in the joints of coarse masonry to protect the mortar joints. They are stuck in while the mortar is wet.
n. 跗关节, 马脚状铁钩, 斜析形屋顶
EN: A symmetrical two-sided roof with two slopes on each side.
EN: A carved stone grotesque with a spout designed to convey water from a roof.
n. 层顶层, 阁楼, 顶楼, 头
EN: A habitable attic at the top of a larger building, generally with sloping walls, and with skylights or dormer windows.
EN: Brickwork constructed of soft bricks rubbed to achieve a fine smooth finish with narrow joints between courses.
EN: A freestanding pavilion structure often found in parks, gardens and public areas.

EN: (Greek: γεῖσον — often interchangeable with cornice) The part of the entablature that projects outward from the top of the frieze in the Doric order and from the top of the frieze course of the Ionic and Corinthian orders; it forms the outer edge of the roof on the sides of a structure with a sloped roof.
EN: On some capitals, a smooth or ornate part placed above the astragalus of a column.

EN: A structure formed of straight wood or metal members between points (or nodes) on a circular sphere (or part thereof) that are "pinned" at each connection point to two or more other members that transfer loads imposed on the structure to the base of the structure. The geometric areas between individual members may support a "skin" if the structure is to be enclosed. A "regular" geodesic structure have members of equal length but strengths of members may vary depending on location in the geodesic "grid".
n. 洞穴, 岩穴, 洞室
EN: An exterior submerged room that is decorated with landscaping or art in which has no exterior exit or entrance. One enters and exits only through the building.
EN: In a Doric entablature, one of a number of small, projecting, drop-like ornaments under the triglyphs between the taenia and the architrave as well as under the mutules.
EN: A type of roof where all sides slope downwards from the ridge to the eaves.
EN: An external moulded projection from a wall over an opening to throw off rainwater. Also known as a dripstone.
EN: Possibly from an older term "heifunon", a structural section connecting the main portion of a building with its projecting "dependencies" or wings.
EN: A row of small figures along the unions of the roofs of Chinese official buildings.
n. 柱子间比率, 柱子间距, 分柱法
EN: The interval separating one column from another in a colonnade. Intercolumniation regularly occurs in six forms: pycnostyle, systyle, eustyle, diastyle, araeostyle, and araeosystyle.

EN: A scheme of decoration employed in Romanesque and Gothic architecture, where arches are thrown from alternate piers, interlacing or intersecting one another. In the former case, the first arch mould is carried alternately over and under the second, in the latter the mouldings actually intersect and stop one another.
[网络] 爱奥尼柱式;爱奥尼克柱式;爱奥尼亚柱式

EN: One of the three orders or organisational systems of Ancient Greek or classical architecture characterised by columns which stood on the flat pavement of a temple with a base, their vertical shafts fluted with parallel concave grooves topped by a capital with volutes, that flared from the column to meet a rectangular abacus with carved ovolo moulding, at the intersection with the horizontal beam that they carried.
EN: A raised surface, platform or terrace upon which an Indian temple is placed.
adj. 乌黑发亮的,煤玉似的
EN: A building technique used in medieval timber frame buildings in which an upper floor projects beyond the dimensions of the floor below.
EN: In Japanese architecture, the upper rail, made from wood, to which shoji or fusuma are attached.

EN: In Japanese architecture, a log used as ornamentation atop the roof. Katsuogi are normally round and are placed in parallel lines perpendicular to the ridge. They are currently only used on Shinto shrines, placed behind chigi and sometimes helping to convey, by their parity, the sex of the kami within.
n. 拱顶石, 楔石, 重点
EN: The architectural piece at the crown of a vault or arch and marks its apex, locking the other pieces into position.
n. 花格平顶, 花格平顶的凹板
EN: The Latin term for a paneled or coffered ceiling, soffit, or vault adorned with a pattern of recessed panels.
EN: An ornamental, lattice framework consisting of small strips in a criss-crossed pattern.
EN: A type of pilaster that lacks a base or capital.
n. 光, 光亮, 灯, 日光, 发光体, 光源, 杰出人物, 火花, 眼光
